page: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs powered by x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at up to 3.7 GHz. The hardware layout includes 1536.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is non-local, requiring network-attached EBS volumes, and network throughput provides a baseline bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The instance contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight high computational and memory throughput across distributed and parallel tasks. In multi-core stress testing, stress-ng recorded 588964.61, placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, matched by a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 143337.26. Read-only uncached large-block memory bandwidth reached 652.3 GB/sec, while write operations measured 309.09 GB/sec. Redis SET operations achieved 323.08 million operations per second, alongside 109.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput, reflecting exceptional capacity for memory-resident transactions.

Performance trade-offs appear in workloads requiring dedicated acceleration or localized I/O. Without onboard local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, single-threaded throughput and sequential generation tasks face constraints. While small-model prompt ingestion reached 4194.28 tokens per second on CPU execution, small-model text generation dropped to 64.02 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 25 percent. The platform maximizes cost efficiency by pooling massive memory density and wide parallelism into a single host footprint, eliminating the need to scale horizontally across multiple smaller nodes.

The r7a.48xlarge is designed for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed in-memory data grids, large Redis clusters, high-concurrency software compilation, and broad data transformation pipelines that require high memory capacity without local hardware acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.48xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs on AMD EPYC 9R14 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz, built on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and supports 50 Gbps baseline network throughput. Local storage is not included, requiring external storage volumes, and there are no GPUs present. Performance benchmarks show top-decile throughput in multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng (588964.61) and PassMark (143337.26), alongside memory bandwidth reaching 652.3 GB/sec on uncached reads. Transactional capabilities are reinforced by 323.08 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Given its 1.5 TB memory allocation and dedicated compute density, this instance is suited for massive in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, and high-concurrency compilation pipelines.
